# nwc-kit

> Small, security-focused Nostr Wallet Connect client for TypeScript. Implements the NIP-47 core with NIP-44 v2 encryption and authenticated wallet responses, so an application can spend through a constrained connection to an existing Lightning wallet. Not a wallet, custody layer, policy engine or invoice verifier.

Live demo and documentation: https://nwc-kit.forgesworn.dev
GitHub: https://github.com/forgesworn/nwc-kit
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@forgesworn/nwc-kit

**Early 0.x release.** Verified against the NIP-44 protocol vectors, an adversarial fake wallet, and a controlled mainnet acceptance through Rizful in the 402-mcp payment path. That proves one wallet and provider path, not every real-world implementation. The API may move within 0.x; pin an exact version.

ESM-only. Node 22+, browsers, Deno and Bun. No `node:` imports. One runtime dependency: `nostr-tools`. Two subpath exports: `@forgesworn/nwc-kit` (main), `@forgesworn/nwc-kit/extensions/05` (transaction history).

**All NIP-47 amount, balance and fee fields are integers in milli-satoshis.** Convert sats explicitly at the application boundary.

## Install

npm install @forgesworn/nwc-kit

The Usage example also uses `farrier-kit` (an application dependency, not a dependency of `nwc-kit`): npm install farrier-kit

## Subpath Exports

### @forgesworn/nwc-kit (main entry)

Classes:
- `new NwcClient(connectionUri, options?)`: options are `{ transport?: NwcTransport, requestTimeoutMs?: number, infoTimeoutMs?: number, now?: () => number }`. Default request timeout 60000ms, info timeout 10000ms; both must be 100 to 300000ms. `now` returns Unix seconds and defaults to the system clock. Throws `NwcError` `INVALID_CONNECTION` for a bad URI
- `new NostrRelayTransport(pool?: SimplePool)`: the default transport. `SimplePool` is the class from `nostr-tools/pool`; when omitted it uses `new SimplePool({ enableReconnect: true })`. Pass your own pool to configure it
- `NwcError`: extends `Error`, `{ code: NwcErrorCode, message: string, walletCode?: string }`. `walletCode` is set only when `code` is `WALLET_ERROR`

NwcClient methods:
- `connect() → Promise<NwcCapabilities>`: fetches the signed kind-13194 info event, requires `nip44_v2`, caches the result. Optional: every request method calls it implicitly when `capabilities` is `undefined`, so call it yourself only to read `capabilities.methods` before spending or to handle discovery errors separately. It is read-only, so any error from it precedes every request. It can be called again to refresh the cache
- `payInvoice({ invoice, amount?, metadata? }, options?) → Promise<PayInvoiceResult>`: `invoice` is a BOLT-11 string. `amount` is an optional positive integer in milli-satoshis, meant for amountless invoices only. The client forwards it unchecked, does not decode the invoice and cannot tell whether the invoice already has an amount; what a wallet does with both is up to the wallet. Resolves only with a 64-character hex preimage, otherwise throws `INVALID_RESPONSE` (an empty preimage is refused, and that is an ambiguous outcome, not a failed payment)
- `makeInvoice({ amount, description?, description_hash?, expiry?, metadata? }, options?) → Promise<NwcTransaction>`: `amount` is a positive integer in milli-satoshis. `expiry` is a positive integer in seconds. Give `description` or `description_hash` (32-byte hex), not both
- `lookupInvoice({ payment_hash? | invoice? }, options?) → Promise<NwcTransaction>`: exactly one of the two, `payment_hash` as 32-byte hex
- `getBalance(options?) → Promise<GetBalanceResult>`
- `getInfo(options?) → Promise<GetInfoResult>`
- `close() → void`: cancels pending requests with `CLIENT_CLOSED`, zeroises owned key material and clears `capabilities`. Every later call throws `CLIENT_CLOSED`
- `capabilities`: getter, `NwcCapabilities | undefined`
- `walletPubkey`, `clientPubkey`, `relays`: readonly

Request methods validate their parameters first (`INVALID_REQUEST`), then run discovery if needed, then refuse a method the wallet did not list in its info event (`UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`), then publish. `execute` is internal (protected) and not part of the API.

Request options: `{ signal?: AbortSignal, timeoutMs?: number }`. `timeoutMs` must be 100 to 300000.

Functions:
- `inspectNwcConnection(uri) → NwcConnectionInfo`: never returns the secret

Constants:
- `NWC_INFO_KIND`: 13194
- `NWC_REQUEST_KIND`: 23194
- `NWC_RESPONSE_KIND`: 23195

Error codes (`NwcErrorCode`): INVALID_CONNECTION, CLIENT_CLOSED, INFO_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION, UNSUPPORTED_METHOD, UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION, INVALID_REQUEST, PUBLISH_FAILED, RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, REQUEST_ABORTED, INVALID_RESPONSE, WALLET_ERROR

Types: GetBalanceResult, GetInfoResult, LookupInvoiceParams, MakeInvoiceParams, NwcCapabilities, NwcClientOptions, NwcConnectionInfo, NwcCoreMethod, NwcErrorCode, NwcEvent, NwcFilter, NwcPublishResult, NwcRequestOptions, NwcSubscription, NwcTransaction, NwcTransport, PayInvoiceParams, PayInvoiceResult

### Type fields

All amounts, balances and fees are integers in milli-satoshis. Every timestamp is an integer in Unix seconds; a transaction timestamp beyond the year 2100 is refused as `INVALID_RESPONSE` because it is almost certainly milliseconds. In `NwcTransaction` and `GetInfoResult` an unset optional field is omitted, whether the wallet sent it as absent, `null` or `""`.

```ts
interface NwcConnectionInfo { walletPubkey: string; relays: readonly string[]; lud16?: string }

// Returned by connect() and the capabilities getter, copied on each read.
interface NwcCapabilities {
  methods: readonly string[]      // from the info event content, e.g. 'pay_invoice'
  encryptions: readonly string[]  // from the encryption tag; always includes 'nip44_v2'
  extensions: readonly string[]   // from the extensions tag, often empty
  eventId: string                 // id of the signed kind-13194 info event
  createdAt: number               // that event's created_at, Unix seconds
}

interface PayInvoiceResult {
  preimage: string    // 64 lowercase hex characters, never empty
  fees_paid?: number  // milli-satoshis
}

interface GetBalanceResult { balance: number }  // milli-satoshis

// Returned by getInfo(). The wallet's own report, not this client's capability list.
interface GetInfoResult {
  methods: string[]
  extensions?: string[]
  alias?: string
  color?: string
  pubkey?: string       // the wallet's Lightning node id: 66 hex (compressed key) or 64 hex, lowercased
  network?: string
  block_height?: number
  block_hash?: string   // 64 hex, lowercased
}

// Returned by makeInvoice, lookupInvoice and listTransactions.
interface NwcTransaction {
  type?: 'incoming' | 'outgoing'
  state?: 'pending' | 'settled' | 'accepted' | 'expired' | 'failed'
  invoice?: string
  description?: string
  description_hash?: string  // 64 hex
  preimage?: string          // 64 hex, absent when the wallet sends none (for example before settlement)
  payment_hash?: string      // 64 hex
  amount?: number            // milli-satoshis
  fees_paid?: number         // milli-satoshis
  created_at?: number
  expires_at?: number
  settled_at?: number
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
}

interface PayInvoiceParams { invoice: string; amount?: number /* msat */; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }
interface MakeInvoiceParams { amount: number /* msat */; description?: string; description_hash?: string; expiry?: number /* seconds */; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }
interface LookupInvoiceParams { payment_hash?: string; invoice?: string }
interface NwcClientOptions { transport?: NwcTransport; requestTimeoutMs?: number; infoTimeoutMs?: number; now?: () => number }
interface NwcRequestOptions { signal?: AbortSignal; timeoutMs?: number }
```

### Injecting a transport

`NwcTransport` is what `NwcClientOptions.transport` accepts. The default is `NostrRelayTransport`. Implement it for tests or a runtime without a global `WebSocket`. The client verifies every event itself, so a transport only moves events and must not be relied on to authenticate them.

```ts
interface NwcEvent { id: string; pubkey: string; created_at: number; kind: number; tags: string[][]; content: string; sig: string }
interface NwcFilter { ids?: string[]; kinds?: number[]; authors?: string[]; limit?: number; [tag: `#${string}`]: string[] | undefined }
interface NwcSubscription { close(reason?: string): void }
interface NwcPublishResult { relay: string; accepted: boolean }

interface NwcTransport {
  query(relays: readonly string[], filter: NwcFilter, timeoutMs: number): Promise<NwcEvent[]>
  subscribe(
    relays: readonly string[],
    filter: NwcFilter,
    handlers: { onevent(event: NwcEvent): void; onclose?(): void },
    signal?: AbortSignal,
  ): NwcSubscription
  publish(relays: readonly string[], event: NwcEvent, timeoutMs: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<NwcPublishResult[]>
  close(relays: readonly string[]): void
}
```

### @forgesworn/nwc-kit/extensions/05

Draft NWC extension 05, transaction history. Isolated so the core export cannot depend on a draft.

- `new NwcTransactionHistoryClient(connectionUri, options?)`: extends `NwcClient`, same options, so every core method is available too
- `listTransactions(params?: ListTransactionsParams, options?) → Promise<{ transactions: NwcTransaction[] }>`

Exports: `NwcTransactionHistoryClient` and the type `ListTransactionsParams`. `NwcTransaction` comes from the main entry.

```ts
interface ListTransactionsParams {
  from?: number      // Unix seconds, integer >= 0
  until?: number     // Unix seconds, integer >= 0; from must not be after until
  limit?: number     // integer 1 to 20, default 20
  offset?: number    // integer >= 0
  unpaid?: boolean   // forwarded to the wallet unchanged
  type?: 'incoming' | 'outgoing'
}
```

Every invalid parameter throws `INVALID_REQUEST` before anything is sent. A `limit` above 20 is rejected, not clamped. An explicit `limit` is always sent, defaulting to 20, because the extension advises clients to page by at most 20 and wallets otherwise apply a larger default of their own. A response with more transactions than `limit` throws `INVALID_RESPONSE`. The wallet must advertise extension `05` or list `list_transactions` as a method, otherwise the call throws `UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION`. The method must also be listed, otherwise `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`.

## Usage

```ts
import { NwcClient, NwcError } from '@forgesworn/nwc-kit'
import { tryDecodeBolt11, verifyPreimage } from 'farrier-kit'

declare function loadNwcUriFromPrivateStorage(): Promise<string>

// Raised before the request is published: nothing reached the wallet.
const NOT_SENT = new Set([
  'INVALID_CONNECTION', 'INVALID_REQUEST', 'UNSUPPORTED_METHOD',
  'UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION', 'UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION', 'INFO_UNAVAILABLE',
])
// A signed, explicit refusal by the wallet.
const REFUSED = new Set([
  'PAYMENT_FAILED', 'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE', 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED',
  'RATE_LIMITED', 'RESTRICTED', 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED',
])

function classify(error: NwcError): 'not-sent' | 'refused' | 'ambiguous' {
  if (NOT_SENT.has(error.code)) return 'not-sent'
  if (error.code === 'WALLET_ERROR' && REFUSED.has(error.walletCode ?? '')) return 'refused'
  // Timeout, abort, publish failure, close, INVALID_RESPONSE, and WALLET_ERROR
  // with INTERNAL, OTHER or any other code: the payment may have happened.
  return 'ambiguous'
}

// Retrieve the URI from app-owned private storage. Never hard-code or log it.
const connectionUri = await loadNwcUriFromPrivateStorage()
const client = new NwcClient(connectionUri)
const invoice = 'lnbc...'
let payRequested = false

try {
  const capabilities = await client.connect()
  if (!capabilities.methods.includes('pay_invoice')) throw new Error('cannot pay')

  const decoded = tryDecodeBolt11(invoice)
  if (!decoded || decoded.amountMsats === null) throw new Error('bad or amountless invoice')

  payRequested = true
  const result = await client.payInvoice({ invoice })
  if (!verifyPreimage(result.preimage, decoded.paymentHashHex)) {
    // The wallet claimed success, so this is not evidence of non-payment.
    throw new Error('wallet response does not settle this invoice')
  }
} catch (error) {
  if (!(error instanceof NwcError)) throw error
  const outcome = payRequested ? classify(error) : 'not-sent'
  console.error(`payment ${outcome}: ${error.code} ${error.walletCode ?? ''}`)
  // 'ambiguous': reconcile with the wallet before any retry. A blind retry can pay twice.
} finally {
  client.close()
}
```

The amountless check above is this example's own policy, not a library rule: `payInvoice` accepts an amountless invoice if you pass `amount` in milli-satoshis.

## Security Model

- The relay is untrusted. Subscription filters are performance hints, not authentication. Every response is shape-checked, signature-verified and matched to the live request before decryption.
- Wallet author, request reference, client recipient and result method are all checked before a result is trusted.
- A valid wallet event that does not reference the active request is treated as a possible relay replay and ignored.
- NIP-44 v2 is required. Legacy NIP-04 is refused.
- The NWC connection URI is a spending capability. The library never logs or returns it. `close()` zeroises the library-owned secret and conversation-key byte arrays; JavaScript strings cannot be erased, so the caller still owns the URI string.
- Once a payment request is published, **every** failure short of an explicit wallet refusal is an ambiguous outcome, never proof of non-payment: `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`, `REQUEST_ABORTED`, `PUBLISH_FAILED`, `CLIENT_CLOSED` and `INVALID_RESPONSE`. Reconcile the invoice before retrying; a blind retry can pay twice.
- `INVALID_RESPONSE` on a payment looks like a refusal and is not one. It means the wallet answered claiming a result that could not be trusted (bad preimage, wrong `result_type`, undecryptable payload). A real bridge returned an empty preimage as a *successful* result when its node could not route the payment. Rejecting that response is a statement about the evidence, not about the money.
- `WALLET_ERROR` carries the wallet's own code in `walletCode`. Only an explicit refusal is definite: `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `RESTRICTED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. `INTERNAL`, `OTHER` and any unrecognised or missing code (reported as `OTHER`) are ambiguous: reconcile before retrying.
- Apart from an explicit refusal, only failures raised **before** publication prove nothing was attempted: `INVALID_CONNECTION`, `INVALID_REQUEST`, `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`, `UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION`, `UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION`, `INFO_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Passing tests are not evidence that money settled. Verify the invoice before paying and verify the returned preimage against the invoice payment hash afterwards: `farrier-kit` does both.

## Not In Scope

Wallet or node implementation, custody, balances or subwallet management, forward secrecy beyond NIP-44, BOLT-11 / LNURL / L402 / Cashu / WebLN / fiat functionality, legacy NIP-04 interoperability, amount policy, user approval and settlement verification.
